title: Unsupported Operation Exception querying Frozen Tier data
body:
### Elasticsearch Version

8.12.0

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

Elastic Cloud

### Problem Description

I have an ILM policy with 10 days hot, 80 days frozen. Getting partial results for certain queries. Bounding the query with a date range filter to just hot data produces no errors.




### Steps to Reproduce

For context, an excerpt of the mapping:
```
{
    "dynamic" : "strict",
    "properties" : {
      "@participant1" : {
        "type" : "date",
        "format" : "date_optional_time||epoch_millis"
      },
      "request_id" : {
        "type" : "keyword",
        "index" : true
      },
      "customer_id" : {
        "type" : "keyword",
        "index" : true
      },
      "ip_address" : {
        "type" : "ip",
        "index" : true
      },
...
}
```

If I do an non-time bounded query, as simple as the following, I get partial results:

```
GET /<my-data-stream>/_search
{
    "query": {
        "bool": {
            "filter": [
                {
                    "term": {
                        "customer_id": {
                            "value": "some_value"
                        }
                    }
                },
                {
                    "term": {
                        "ip_address": {
                            "value": "10.0.0.0/32"
                        }
                    }
                }
            ]
        }
    },
    "size": 5,
    "sort": [
        {
            "request_id": {
                "order": "desc"
            }
        }
    ]
}
```

The response metadata shows:
```
    "total": 114,
    "successful": 92,
    "skipped": 0,
    "failed": 22,
```

And the failed section shows many of these for difference partial indices that are in the frozen tier (excerpt):
```
      {
        "shard": 0,
        "index": "partial-.<index-name>-2024.01.19-000006",
        "node": "<node>",
        "reason": {
          "type": "unsupported_operation_exception",
          "reason": "unsupported_operation_exception: null"
        }
      },
```

comments.body:
> Does the query work without the "sort"?

Yes, without the sort the query succeeds. With the sort, it executes quickly and fails for the frozen tier data.

> Do the frozen indices have "keyword" mapping for request_id ?

Yes. calling GET  _mapping on one of the partial indices shows the `request_id` field as:
```
        "request_id": {
```

comments.body: This looks to be a limitation around querying the frozen tier that has been around for a long time. comments.body: Having spent more time on this, I apologize because the suggestion around `pre_filter_shard_size` was incorrect! Only removing the primary sort on a keyword would fix that. The core of the issue is that we are playing tricks to try and skip shards, but that should never cause failures. If there is an exception for any reason, we should always fallback to executing the query like we would without any skipping. I opened a PR to fix this at #117469 .
